title: Rigveda 10.166: Against rivals in love
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.166: Against rivals in love: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.166 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to against rivals in love. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 143r-143v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
This manuscript inserts khila verses (supplementary hymns outside Aufrecht's text) at some hymn ends; they are noted in the section notes and not reproduced.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.166.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 143r
translation.original_text:
1ṛ̱ṣa̱bham mā̍ samā̱nānā̍ṁ sa̱patnā̍nāṁ viṣāsa̱him | ha̱ntāra̱ṁ śatrū̍ṇāṁ kṛdhi vi̱rāja̱ṁ gopa̍ti̱ṁ gavā̍m ||
2a̱ham a̍smi sapatna̱hendra̍ i̱vāri̍ṣṭo̱ akṣa̍taḥ | a̱dhaḥ sa̱patnā̍ me pa̱dor i̱me sarve̍ a̱bhiṣṭhi̍tāḥ ||
3atrai̱va vo 'pi̍ nahyāmy u̱bhe ārtnī̍ iva̱ jyayā̍ | vāca̍s pate̱ ni ṣe̍dhe̱mān yathā̱ mad adha̍ra̱ṁ vadā̍n ||
translation.text:
1MAKE me a bull among my peers, make me my rivals, conqueror: Make me the slayer of my foes, a sovran ruler, lord of kine
2I am my rivals' slayer, like Indra unwounded and unhurt, And all these enemies of mine are vanquished and beneath my feet.
3Here, verily, I bind you fast, as the two bow-ends with the string. Press down these men, O Lord of Speech, that they may humbly speak to me.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 143r (OPenn image 142, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.165.4 ‹-namo astu mṛtyave›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 143v, begins in RV 10.166.4 ‹-vaś cittam ā vo›. Verses 10.166.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.166.4-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 143v
translation.original_text:
4a̱bhi̱bhūr a̱ham āga̍maṁ vi̱śvaka̍rmeṇa̱ dhāmnā̍ | ā va̍ś ci̱ttam ā vo̍ vra̱tam ā vo̱ 'haṁ sami̍tiṁ dade ||
5yo̱ga̱kṣe̱maṁ va̍ ā̱dāyā̱ham bhū̍yāsam utta̱ma ā vo̍ mū̱rdhāna̍m akramīm | a̱dha̱spa̱dān ma̱ ud va̍data ma̱ṇḍūkā̍ ivoda̱kān ma̱ṇḍūkā̍ uda̱kād i̍va ||
translation.text:
4Hither I came as conqueror with mighty all-effecting power, And I have mastered all your thought, your synod, and your holy work.
5May I be highest, having gained your strength in war, your skill in peace my feet have trodden on your heads. Speak to me from beneath my feet, as frogs from out the water croak, as frogs from out the water croak.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 143v (OPenn image 143, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.166.4 ‹-vaś cittam ā vo›. 10.166.5 ends in line 3 with a varga number, followed by the heading khilaṃ and khila verses (yenedaṃ bhūtaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhaviṣyat, the Sivasamkalpa), which run to 146r line 3. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 146r, begins in RV 10.167.1 ‹tubhyedam indra pari ṣicyate›. Verses 10.166.4-5 end on this page; 10.166.4 begins on fol. 143r.
